newsitem.title: USA: PGA GOLF-HAAS AND KITE WIN SHARK SHOOTOUT.
newsitem.headline: PGA GOLF-HAAS AND KITE WIN SHARK SHOOTOUT.

text.p: Jay Haas and
Tom Kite combined to shoot a 12-under-par 60 for a two-stroke
victory at the $1.1 million Shark Shootout golf tournament
Sunday.
Haas and Kite, who placed sixth last year, finished with
a three-day total of 29-under 187. They split the $300,000
first prize.
The teams of Craig Stadler and Lanny Wadkins, the
second-round leaders, and Hale Irwin and Lee Janzen finished
tied for second at 27-under 189. Stadler and Wadkins carded a
63 and Irwin and Janzen combined for a 60.
Mark O'Meara and Curtis Strange tied Brad Faxon and Peter
Jacobsen for fourth place at 26-under. O'Meara and Strange,
who held a share of the lead after the first round, fired a
60 while Faxon and Jacobsen carded a 59.
Chip Beck and Scott Hoch finished in sole possession of
sixth place at 22-under after a 59.
Sunday's final round was a scramble in which each player
hit a tee shot and the team then selected the best ball. Both
players then hit their second shot from the spot of the best
ball and continued the process until the hole was complete.
Australia's Greg Norman still remains winless in the
tournament he hosts, as he and two-time champion Raymond
Floyd placed seventh, along with 1996 Senior Tour money
champion Jim Colbert and Bruce Lietzke at 20-under.
Rounding out the 10-team field were defending champions
Steve Elkington and Mark Calcavecchia at 19-under and John
Daly and David Duval at 18-under.
Elkington was trying to become the first member of a team
to win three times. Last year, he and Calcavecchia combined
for a 32-under 184 and a six-stroke victory over the tandem
of Faxon and Fred Couples.
Elkington, who finished 42nd on the money list this year,
previously won the crown in 1993 with Floyd, who also won in
1990 with Couples. Couples and Faxon won in 1994.
The Sherwood Country Club course is a par-72, 7,025-yard
layout.
